title: Ebola treatments trial begins in DR Congo
facts: The World Health Organization announced the beginning of a trial of potential treatments for the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The first patient for the Ebola treatments trial has been enrolled in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is caused by the Bundibugyo virus species.
There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo virus species of Ebola.
The Ebola treatments trial is sponsored by the World Health Organization.
Scientists at the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale in the Democratic Republic of Congo are co-ordinating the trial alongside international partners.
The current outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo began in May.
The World Health Organization has declared the current Ebola situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo a public health emergency.
The World Health Organization reported 1,460 confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo as of July 1, 2026.
The World Health Organization reported 452 deaths from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo as of July 1, 2026.
Ugandan authorities have confirmed 20 cases of Ebola.
The current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is concentrated in the South Kivu, North Kivu, and Ituri provinces.
A pregnant woman in the Tshopo province of the Democratic Republic of Congo tested positive for Ebola after dying in Ituri.
Public gatherings were banned in the Tshopo, Haut-Uele, and Bas-Uele provinces and the capital Kinshasa to prevent the spread of Ebola.
The number of laboratories testing for Ebola in the affected region of the Democratic Republic of Congo has increased from four to ten.
